extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers / researchers who are asked to review manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: A short, practical four-step rubric advising researchers on how to behave when asked to peer-review manuscripts so reviews are constructive, fair, and useful. Focuses on when to accept reviews, tone, and actionable feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Your Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline reviews when you lack confidence in the methodology or field. You should have "some knowledge of its themes and methods" to competently assess the work's contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not feel confident about the paper's methods or subject area, refuse the assignment rather than providing uninformed or superficial critique. The point is to ensure you can legitimately evaluate the manuscript's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review When Ready
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reviewing the work of your peers should be pleasurable." Don't accept papers when stressed or overcommitted — your negative state will degrade both review quality and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept review requests when you have the time and mental bandwidth to do a thoughtful job. If you are rushed, tired, or overwhelmed, your comments are likely to be lower quality and potentially unnecessarily harsh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice Constructive Kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace accusatory language like "authors clearly aren't aware" with supportive phrasing such as "I'd like to see engagement with theorist X."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that maintains professionalism and encourages improvement rather than provoking defensiveness. Frame critiques as suggestions or requests for engagement, not as indictments of the authors' competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific and Actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague criticism (e.g., "analysis problematic") helps no one. Explain what is problematic, what is missing, and suggest alternatives. Provide complete citations and links when recommending sources so authors can actually find them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete examples of problems, outline missing elements, and propose specific remedies or references. When suggesting literature, include full citations or links to make it easy for authors to follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying Principle: Treat Manuscripts as You'd Want Yours Treated
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat manuscripts with fairness, specificity, and genuine helpfulness — essentially the golden rule for reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let empathy guide review tone and content: be fair, give precise feedback, and aim to genuinely help authors improve their work rather than simply criticize.
